title: WallContract
description: The only interface between the Python pipeline and the frontend. Phase 1 delivers this as a build-time JSON file; a later HTTP API serves the identical shape at the same path, so the frontend does not change.

contract_version.description: Which shape this document is (docs/adr/0024). An added optional field is a minor bump; anything else is major, and a page built for another major refuses to build.

generated_at.description: The knowledge moment this payload reconstructs. Not merely a build timestamp: the store is bitemporal, so a wall can be rebuilt as it stood on any past date.

health.description: When each source group was last reached, as the export saw it: the heartbeat of docs/adr/0023, so a reader can tell fresh data from a collector that has stopped. Null in an as-of export, whose question is a different day. Added in 1.3.0.

latest.description: UTC time of the newest successful fetch, or null if none is on record.

silent.description: Not reached within its limit: the collector for it has stopped, or cannot reach it.

weeks.description: The weekly digest (docs/adr/0039), oldest week first: for each ISO week since collection began, the difference between every series as it could be known at the week's end and at the end of the week before (the as-of rule of docs/adr/0025). A past week reads as it stood then. Added in 1.8.0.

cut.description: The day the snapshot stands on: the Sunday for a week that is over, the export's day for the current one.

moves.description: Daily and weekly series: the latest reading at the cut against the latest at the week before's end. prev_d equal to d means no new reading came out.

prev_d.description: Null when the series was not yet knowable a week earlier.

delta.description: v − prev_v, in the series' unit.

pct.description: Null when either value is at or below zero.

hi.description: The highest daily reading this week; null for a weekly series or fewer than two days.

released.description: Monthly, quarterly and annual series: periods that came out during the week (past the latest held a week earlier), and periods whose value changed. Ordered by the day each became knowable.

on.description: The release date, or the day this warehouse learned an undated value.

prior_d.description: The period before, at the same cadence.

pct.description: Against the period before; null at or below zero.

revised_from.description: The value held a week earlier for the same period, when this one replaced it.

curve.description: Each listed futures contract's settle at the cut against a week earlier, nearest delivery first.

on.description: The trading day of the settle.

upcoming.description: Releases the calendar (docs/adr/0031) expects within seven days of the cut, or that are overdue. An expectation, never a date.

granularity.description: The cadence of the period expected: the latest reading's.

market.description: The futures curve's history and the market's track record (docs/adr/0036): every contract's settles by week, and for each delivered contract what it priced 1, 3, 6 and 9 months before its delivery month against its last settle. Arithmetic on settles, no model. Null when no curve is held. Added in 1.7.0.

series.description: The panel these settles are prints of.

delivery.description: The end of the contract's delivery month: its obs_date.

delivered.description: Its delivery month is over and its prints reach it: it has a last settle to be judged against.

d.description: Trading day: the last of its ISO week.

months.description: Months before the delivery month began.

mean_abs_pct.description: Mean distance from the last settle, in percent of it.

mean_pct.description: Mean signed miss: above zero, the market priced higher than the contract finished.

ahead.description: Only the horizons it was listed for.

d.description: The trading day of the settle in force.

panels.description: Ordered by the causal chain: capacity leads price by 10-12 months, margin decides whether a capacity move persists.

name_zh.description: The indicator's name in Chinese, as the registry defines it. Both names are carried because the caliber lives in the name — 定点屠宰量（全口径） and 定点屠宰量（规模以上） are two different measurements, and a frontend-side lookup table would be free to drift from that distinction.

in_wall.description: Whether this series belongs in the causal-chain wall. False for equities: a share price is a claim on the cycle, not a link in it, so it lives in the overlay instead.

forecast.description: A source's projection rather than a measurement: its latest points lie in the future, and it is kept off the wall. Present on every panel; true for USDA's series.

revises.description: Whether this series is watched for restatement after the fact. Set for 能繁母猪存栏, the only real leading indicator. No period has been restated in the 55 primary-source editions held (2021-12 to 2026-07); its release lag is what a backtest has to respect today.

threshold.description: A reference line that means something in the domain, not chart decoration.

about.description: What the series is, for a reader, in both languages (config/about.yaml). Like the names, it travels in the contract because the caliber lives in it. The export fails if any series lacks one; null only in payloads built without config, such as tests.

url.description: A page a reader can check, or null when the only address is an API. Never a guessed page.

revisions.description: Every period whose value changed, with each value in the order it was learned. Empty for most series: a restatement is rare, and this lists only real ones.

p.description: Release date of this value, or null when the source did not say.

learned.description: UTC date this warehouse learned the value (transaction time).

UTC date this warehouse learned the panel's undated points (those without p), unless a point carries its own l. For a source that does not date its releases this is the only bound on when a value was knowable, and the page never assumes an earlier one (docs/adr/0025). Null when every point is dated. Added in 1.1.0.

caliber.description: Where this caliber begins and ends, and the indicators it continues or is continued by: two indicators, never one line, but the chart says at the seam where the other history is (docs/adr/0026). Null when the series has no caliber boundary. Added in 1.2.0.

earlier.description: Id of the indicator whose earlier caliber this continues.

later.description: Id of the indicator that continues this caliber.

breaks.description: Where the series settles into a new cadence, classed by the gap between readings: D, W, M, Q or A. A computed fact, like a streak (docs/adr/0026). Added in 1.2.0.

d.description: The reading the new cadence starts from.

settled.description: The reading that made the new cadence count. Before it was knowable the break was not, so a page standing on an earlier day leaves it out (docs/adr/0025).

release_lag.description: Days from a period's end to its release, over the points that carry p. Null when the source does not date releases. The median is what to subtract from a lead read off the chart; the max is the oldest a reader acting on the latest release has had to work with.

points.description: Ascending by date. Each point keeps its own granularity: this series genuinely mixes annual, quarterly and monthly readings, and flattening them would claim they are equivalent measurements.

p.description: The day the publisher released this value, ISO date. Absent when the source does not date its releases: unknown, never assumed to equal d. Present, it is when the value became usable, which for a monthly print is three to nine weeks after d.

l.description: On an undated point only: the UTC date this warehouse learned it, when that differs from the panel's learned. Added in 1.1.0.

readings.description: Latest value per series with its position in its own history. Context for a human judgement, never a verdict.

in_wall.description: Whether this reading describes the current state of the physical cycle. False for equities (a claim on the cycle, not a measurement of it) and for retired calibers (history, whose last value is not a reading of today).

published_on.description: The day the publisher released the latest value, or null when the source does not say.

history_years.description: Years of history the percentile is taken over, from the series' first observation in the window to its latest. A 4th percentile over 11.7 years and a 24th over 1.1 are different claims, so the page shows the span beside the position. Null when there is no percentile. Added in 1.4.0.

yoy.description: Percent change against the observation nearest one year earlier, or null when none sits near the anniversary. Null is a real answer: a series that began this year has no year-on-year.

stale.description: The series has not advanced within its own cadence as of generated_at. A stale reading is still shown, because hiding it is the silent failure this project exists to avoid, but it must not read as a current level. An upstream_dark acknowledgement in config does not soften this: it quiets the collector's alarm, not the page.

age_days.description: Days from obs_date to generated_at: how far the reader should discount a stale reading.

first_seen.description: UTC date this warehouse first learned the latest observation (transaction time). For a backfilled series it is the backfill date, not the publisher's release date.

extreme.description: Set when the latest value is the lowest or highest the series has been for at least a year. since is the most recent earlier observation at least as extreme, or the window's first observation when all is true. A fact with a fixed definition, never a phase call.

change.description: Percent change from the previous reading of the same granularity, and that reading's date. Null when there is no previous one.

streak.description: Consecutive moves in one direction ending at the latest reading, among readings of its granularity: n moves (at least 2) since the reading where the run began. Null when the latest move is flat or the run is shorter. A count of moves, not a trend call.

threshold_run.description: For a series with a domain threshold: how many consecutive observations sit on the latest value's side of it, and since when. A value on the line counts as above.

next_release.description: When the next period's value is due, read off the series' own dated releases (docs/adr/0031): the period's end plus the median release lag (usual) and plus the longest on record (by). An expectation, never a date: published_on is never filled from it. Overdue when generated_at is past by. Null for an undated, daily, retired or forecast series, or one with fewer than six dated releases. Added in 1.5.0.

period.description: End of the next period, ISO date.
